newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal revenues decline in first 10 months.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal revenues decline in first 10 months.

text.p: Suez Canal revenues continued a downtrend to $1.481 billion in the first 10 months of 1996 from $1.606 billion in the same period last year, the Suez Canal Authority (SCA) statistics department said on Friday.
Revenue from the canal in October alone amounted to $123 million against $153 million in the same month of 1995, it added.
The department said that 12,210 ships used the canal in the first 10 months of 1996. It did not give comparative figures.
Revenues from the Suez Canal form one of the four major foreign currency earners in Egypt.
The SCA decided to keep the transit tolls unchanged for 1997, the third year in a row, an SCA economic unit official told Reuters.
The authority, facing severe competition from other marine and land routes, is even expected to offer new toll discounts to encourge the use of the canal, said the official, who asked anonymity.
